page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a baseline clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance delivers average multi-core performance but exhibits weaker single-core capabilities. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, single-core performance falls into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression is categorized as poor. However, multi-threaded operations, including multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 decompression, consistently rank in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also demonstrate average performance, aligning with its memory-optimized hardware profile.

Given its high memory capacity relative to compute resources, the ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring large memory footprints without demanding extreme single-thread CPU performance. It is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and software compilation, all of which achieved average ratings in benchmark testing. Conversely, it is less optimal for single-threaded processing tasks or large-scale LLM inference due to its weaker single-core execution speeds.
